verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The repository has no declaration defining a seminorm |V|_m as a pointwise maximum over multi-indices; the role of (5.23) is played by the operator norm ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m V x‖ of the full m-th Fréchet derivative on spacetime, used inside JetRate/FiniteJetRate. Recovery, on the 4-dimensional spacetime: each ∂_x^α ∂_t^b V with |α|+b = m is D^m V evaluated at m coordinate unit vectors, so max_{|α|+b=m} |∂_x^α ∂_t^b V| ≤ ‖D^m V‖; conversely expanding D^m V multilinearly in the coordinate basis gives ‖D^m V‖ ≤ 4^m · max_{|α|+b=m} |∂_x^α ∂_t^b V|. FiniteJetRate quantifies ∀ m ≤ M under one constant C, which is the same as bounding the max over |α|+b ≤ M, and every use of |·|_m in the manuscript is inside an estimate ≤ C q^(…), so the dimensional factor 4^m is absorbed by C. Two further packaging points: the paper's |·|_m applies to a tuple V of fields (max also over the tuple entries) whereas the Lean estimates are stated separately per field; and the Lean q in JetRate is an explicit argument (instantiated as (cartesianChart h z).1) rather than the paper's fixed similarity coordinate.
